# Storage boundary type census

Revision: `1b18e26491860b644f6e7373bc554e814cf95b66`. Source observation completed 2026-10-27 12:58 UTC. Task: `work-1793104264984144896-34`.

This is a source census and design review, not a runtime bug report. It covers every tracked path in the assigned runtime-store/runtime-schema roots mechanically and dispositions every candidate family found by that scan. It does **not** claim every line was manually read. Relevant producer, decoder, schema and consumer bodies were deeply inspected as identified per row; several families explicitly retain a deeper-proof gap. No builds, tests, installs, edits, application starts, filesystem state-directory reads, model requests or live services were used. All witnesses below are proposed and unrun. The known unrelated Linux compile issue was not used as evidence.

The useful distinction is actual typed ownership versus a typed-looking wrapper. There are **24 concrete JsonRecord types**: **16 macro Value carriers**, **5 id-plus-flattened-Value carriers**, **AgentRecord and WorkItemRecord with partially typed operational fields**, and **one concrete ProfileRecord DTO**. The generic table first parses Value, validates a schema, and then often deserializes that Value. A call spelled from_str::<TaskRecord> still parses Value inside the wrapper. Changing that spelling alone would not establish typed ownership.

Family dispositions: **68 rows: 32 D, 17 R, 9 T, 10 U**. These are refactoring dispositions, not defect counts. A D row means the owned envelope can be decoded directly once the stated compatibility/refinement contract is represented; opaque leaves and essential dynamic checks remain. Several rows deliberately cover related variants under one named owner; no top-N selection was applied.

Aliases for evidence: **S** = workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-store/src; **H** = workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-schema/src; **V** = workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-services/src; **P** = workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-providers/src; **HTTP** = workspaces/runtime/packages/runtime-http/src. All line references refer to the fixed revision. External caller files were followed for evidence, not included as a full census of those external roots.

## Decode feasibility and checks that survive

For ordinary Table records, records.rs:633,1075,1084,1217 reads SQLite **TEXT**, validates UTF-8 and then parses JSON. An owned DTO can use serde_json::from_str directly on that text (or from_slice on its UTF-8 bytes), retaining table/key error context. Generic get_json_record<T>/decode_json_record<T> at records.rs:1291 already provide direct generic deserialization; selecting T=Value or a macro Value wrapper does not make a structural DTO.

For compressed storage, stored_text.rs is the format owner. StoredText first verifies/decompresses TEXT-or-BLOB and yields text; only then is direct DTO parsing feasible. Do not parse compressed BLOB bytes as JSON. stored_text_compaction.rs owns runtime_item_fulltext.body and analytics_items.record; stored_text_dictionary.rs owns the immutable trained dictionaries and temp.analytics_items decoding view. Unqualified reads can therefore see text while writes target main.analytics_items. Arbitrary fulltext is not a JSON candidate.

A future typed reader must explicitly preserve: missing versus null; defaults only on omission; required-nullable fields; extension openness; historical variants; duplicate-key policy (Value can collapse duplicates while derived struct decoding may reject them); raw ordering/signature/hash behavior; numeric bounds/finite values/safe integer units; stable diagnostic context; and row-column/payload identity. Deserialize alone proves none of epoch freshness, permissions, filesystem state, replay safety, successful side effects, budget charge uniqueness, cross-row consistency or valid transitions. Remove shape checks only when an owned type/refined constructor represents the same check.

The strongest concrete source discrepancy is ProfileRecord: S/repositories/profiles.rs:27 denies unknown fields, while H/schemas/persisted-profile-record.schema.json:5,8 permits them and says future fields remain readable. This is a confirmed declaration mismatch, with an unrun extra-field repository witness; no observed user failure is asserted.

No strict current-envelope-only parser. | Bare legacy receipt and modern envelope through load→replay, missing metadata, wrong request/account/signature and transient URL redaction. |

## Remaining proof boundaries and handoff

The ten U families are explicitly not implementation-ready whole-family conversions: F02 Agent records, volatile overlay and agent lifecycle projections; F12 Terminal record and terminal request receipts; F23 Graph-agent records; F27 Projects, locations, peer teams and sidebar state; F28 Normalized queue events and embedded event-kind data; F34 Account limit observations and workspace rate-limit hydration; F42 Rooms, groups, chat messages and deliveries; F47 Analytics history/importer and repair metadata; F49 Legacy budget state and budget-usage receipts; F63 Claude failure stored leaf projection. Their unknowns are identified in their rows rather than hidden behind a claim of total manual review. In particular the whole agent extension universe, every historical terminal/queue/graph/chat shape, tolerant account-limit hydration, generic project/sidebar acceptance, historical budget writers, metadata key variants and Claude failure sanitization need deeper proof.

The broad String/Option sweep did not classify every string as an enum candidate. Stable closed sets were found for voice kinds/session/playback, access client/invite, server delivery state, tool request stage/outcome and policy-owned operation phases. AgentStatus::Other, provider/model/effort identifiers, CacheReport.ttl future values, human command stage, error messages, path/id/hash strings and raw provider variants have different contracts. Required-nullable profile effort, queue Field<T>, volatile overlay nulls, raw signature fields and partial rate observation semantics must stay distinct.

All 203 production/source-schema paths have family IDs in the persisted fileCoverage array; no source path remains unmapped. Files classified T/R or grouped infrastructure were mechanically fully scanned and selected relevant constructors were inspected; this is not a claim of exhaustive manual proof of all business behavior. Dedicated test/fixture sources were inventoried/scanned as evidence sources, not executed. Source findings do not establish performance improvement or runtime failure until a relevant caller witness is implemented and run under a separately authorized change.
